atoms.1: When discontinuing fluoxetine (Prozac), a gradual tapering of the dose is generally recommended to minimize the risk of withdrawal symptoms.
atoms.2: The American Psychiatric Association recommends a gradual tapering of the dose over a period of 2-4 weeks.
atoms.3: A gradual tapering of the dose allows the body to adjust to the decrease in medication levels.
atoms.4: A gradual tapering of the dose reduces the risk of withdrawal symptoms.
atoms.5: Possible withdrawal symptoms include dizziness, headaches, and irritability.
atoms.6: The exact tapering schedule may vary depending on the individual's response to the medication.
atoms.7: The exact tapering schedule may vary depending on the severity of their symptoms.
atoms.8: A healthcare provider may recommend a specific tapering schedule.
atoms.9: A specific tapering schedule may involve reducing the dose by 10-20% every 1-2 weeks.
atoms.10: It is essential to work closely with a healthcare provider to determine the best tapering schedule for your specific situation.
atoms.11: Abruptly stopping fluoxetine can lead to withdrawal symptoms.
atoms.12: Abruptly stopping fluoxetine can lead to dizziness.
atoms.13: Abruptly stopping fluoxetine can lead to headaches.
atoms.14: Abruptly stopping fluoxetine can lead to irritability.
atoms.15: Abruptly stopping fluoxetine can lead to flu-like symptoms.
atoms.16: In severe cases, withdrawal from fluoxetine can lead to more serious symptoms.
atoms.17: In severe cases, withdrawal from fluoxetine can lead to seizures.
atoms.18: In severe cases, withdrawal from fluoxetine can lead to serotonin syndrome.
